sent_subject: Two quick fixes to turn paid clicks into booked demos at LayerLock (+ 10‑min GEM checklist)
sent:
Nina —

If clicks aren’t turning into booked demos, it’s usually two levers: the opener on the demo page and over‑segmented ads fighting learning. Here’s the fastest pass at both.

10‑minute Meta GEM checklist
- Optimise to one thing: Booked demo. Make sure that event fires on the thank‑you state, not just “lead submitted.”
- Let GEM learn: run placements across Feed/Stories/Reels/IG and avoid splitting into many ad sets.
- Feed it concepts in threes: (1) 20–30s product‑in‑use clip, (2) quick founder phone demo, (3) proof‑first graphic. Kill any variant after ~3 weeks of falling CTR.
- Exclude existing customers/recent submitters; keep retargeting separate.
- UTMs that label concept + variant, so you can see which creative actually books demos.

Demo‑page mini‑fix (the change that helped halve cost per demo at Ledgerly)
- Lead with the first question prospects ask on calls. Put the direct answer in the first screen, then 3 short proofs (e.g., compliance/security, time to deploy, who uses it daily).
- One action only: “Book a 15‑min demo.” Form: Name, Work email, Role, Organisation. Anything else moves below the fold.
- Add one trust element above the fold (logo, short quote, or stat). Keep the rest for below.

LinkedIn in 15 minutes
- Two audiences only: Core (relevant job titles/functions) and Warm (site visitors/video viewers). Move budget to whichever books demos this week.
- One concept, three variants. Replace only when CTR slides for ~3 weeks.

Side note: I couldn’t open layerlock.example just now — could you share the correct URL or a working link to your demo page? I’ll point out the first five fixes and how to lay out a one‑screen version you can ship fast.

Fieldwork Studio
